description: You are a Security Engineer who has just onboarded two new infrastructure components — an nginx web server and a PostgreSQL database server — into the company's monitored environment. Log files from these sources exist on the endpoints but Wazuh has no decoder pipeline for either source, meaning web attacks and database access violations are going entirely undetected. Your goal is to build a complete multi-source log ingestion and detection pipeline. The end state must include: (1) a parent-child decoder pair in Wazuh's local_decoder.xml for nginx access log format, correctly parsing at minimum the source IP address, HTTP method, URL path, and HTTP status code fields; (2) a parent-child decoder pair for PostgreSQL log format, parsing at minimum the database name, user, and event/error type; (3) at least 3 detection rules total — at least one targeting nginx web attack patterns (SQL injection, path traversal, directory scanning, or HTTP error anomalies) and at least one targeting PostgreSQL unauthorized access or authentication failures; (4) ossec.conf updated with localfile entries pointing to the nginx and PostgreSQL log file locations; and (5) the existing web-servers agent group's shared agent.conf updated to apply these monitoring settings to all web-servers group members. Sample nginx and PostgreSQL log files have been staged in the system for reference. Log in to the Wazuh dashboard at https://localhost with username admin, password SecretPassword.
